title: Postdeploy throughput regression playbook
content:
TL;DR: After the Jan 14 deploy (runtime: v2.13.0, batching heuristic tweak), we observed a ~22% drop in sustained throughput on 8-GPU pools serving mix-A requests around 13:00 UTC. Latency p95 remained mostly stable, but queue depth and cpu-side wait rose; suspected misconfiguration in continuous batching window/eviction and an unexpected interaction with KV cache TTL.

Known symptoms (observed):
- QPS stable or slightly lower (~5%), token/sec down ~22% on mix-A (longer context), measured by token_out / min over 1h windows.
- CPU wait and scheduler runqueue increased on TensorRunner host: runq-sample metrics show spikes correlating with throughput drop.
- Latency p50/p90 steady; p95 up ~40ms for longer sequences. Tail latency spikes aligned with small batches being sent more often.
- Autoscaler did not trigger; utilization per GPU fell under the threshold because per-request time increased (due to repeated warmups).
- KV cache hit rates dropped from ~84% to ~62% starting ~12:55 UTC.

Quick timeline (local notes):
- 2025-01-14 11:30 UTC: Canary passed, merged batching-heuristic branch (PR 476).
- 2025-01-14 12:05 UTC: Full rollout to region-us-west.
- 2025-01-14 12:55 UTC: First customer alert: throughput drop reported for workspace-azimuth.
- 2025-01-14 13:10 UTC: SRE pager: investigate. Began digging into runtime logs.
- 2025-01-14 13:25 UTC: Identified increased small-batch frequency matching a change in window drain heuristic.

Commands / queries run (save for reproduction):
- kubectl -n inference logs -l app=serve-runtime --since=2h | grep "batch-window" -A4 -B2
- curl "https://metrics.internal/api/query?query=token_out%7Bpool%3D%22mix-A%22%7D&start=1705210000&end=1705213600" | jq .
- pg_dump of trace events for timeframe: pulled event ids (trace-ids list in linked artifacts).

Key log snippets (redacted):
- [2025-01-14T12:57:11Z] runtime: batch-window: draining due to heuristic: idle_timeout=20ms, current_window=8, seen=3 -> flushing small windows
- [2025-01-14T12:57:11Z] runtime.kv: cache-evict: key-prefix xyz, ttl-ms=60000, reason=manual-sweep
- [2025-01-14T12:57:12Z] scheduler: submit: batch_size=2, slots_request=2, estimated_exec_ms=180, actual_exec_ms=185
- [2025-01-14T13:04:03Z] telemetry: prefix-cache-hit-rate=0.62 (prev=0.84), note=spike in cache invalidation

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Batching window heuristic change increased small-batch flush frequency for infrequent long-context requests, which reduced effective batching and incurred repeated KV cache cold-starts. Result: more repeated token computation and lower throughput.
2) A manual KV cache sweep routine (newly enabled) runs on shift boundaries and evicts prefixes too aggressively; combined with (1) it amplifies cost of small batches.
3) Kernel selection fallback path for sequences >1024 is slightly slower after v2.13.0 due to new vectorized fallback; only affects longer sequences and interacts with batching.
4) Traffic pattern change unrelated to deploy (customer test causing many small real-time queries). Lower priority given lack of correlated traffic origination.

Experiments/troubleshooting performed:
- Reverted heuristic on a single canary: re-deployed older batching config to pool-test-3. Result: token/sec recovered ~18% within 10 minutes on that pool. (evidence strongly supports hypothesis 1)
- Temporarily disabled KV cache sweep cron on a test cluster (by setting env KV_SWEEP_ENABLED=false). Result: small improvement in cache-hit-rate, but not full recovery. (suggests compounding issue)
- Forced longer drain window (config: BATCH_WINDOW_MAX_MS=200) for a subset of requests: mixed results; increased p95 slightly but throughput recovered to ~95% pre-deploy.
- Ran microbenchmarks: long-context workload with and without cache warmup: with cold cache throughput down ~28% vs warmed cache.

Repro recipe (dev):
- Use local runner with loadgen profile: loadgen/long-context-50-rps.json (scripts/loadgen). Set batching_heuristic=postdeploy-variant, kv_ttl=60s, concurrency=8.
- Observe token_out rate and prefix-cache-hit-rate. Re-run with batching_heuristic=predeploy and compare.

Important config snippets captured: (note: configs truncated)
- BATCHING_HEURISTIC: "aggressive-drain-v2"
- BATCH_WINDOW_MAX_MS: "50"
- PREFETCH_KV_TTL_MS: "60000"
- KV_SWEEP_ENABLED: "true"

Open questions / unknowns to resolve:
- What triggered the KV manual sweep around 12:57? Cron? Admin action? Garbage-collector threshold?
- Was there an unobserved traffic spike from a single workspace that changed per-worker arrival patterns? Check ingress logs for ~12:45-13:15 UTC.
- Are there any downstream model changes (tokenizer or model weights) that could change kernel selection heuristics for >1024 sequences?

Immediate next steps (short term):
- Roll back batching heuristic globally to predeploy variant (scheduling note: coordinate with infra for low-risk window). Owner: Maya. ETA: 2025-01-21 02:00 UTC.
- Disable KV sweep for all test clusters and confirm hit-rate recovery. Owner: Diego. ETA: 2025-01-21 04:00 UTC.
- Add a short-lived rate-limited canary for aggressive-drain-v2 with KV_SWEEP_ENABLED=false to isolate effects. Owner: Priya. ETA: 2025-01-21 06:00 UTC.
- Add dashboard panel: per-pool batch-size-distribution (histogram), prefix-cache-hit-rate, and scheduler-runq. Quick Grafana link placeholder: /d/serve/runtime-debug?panel=batch_size_dist

Longer-term actions (post-mitigation):
- Add telemetry: emit event when KV sweep runs and include trigger/source.
- Rework heuristic to consider per-route cold-start penalty (KV miss cost), not just idle time.
- Add an automatic rollback policy if token/sec drops >12% and cache-hit-rate drops >10% within 15m after config rollout.

Notes to self / lessons learned:
- Small changes in drain heuristics have outsized effects when KV caches are warm/cold; we need a synthetic test that exercises the combination before rollout.
- For canaries: test both latency and token-throughput under warmed and cold cache scenarios.
- Keep better provenance of any admin-triggered KV actions; too many manual ops are invisible in current telemetry.

Raw snippets / quick traces: (kept for context)
- trace-id: 8f3a-77c1b - event: window-flush (size=2) -> cause=heuristic_draining
- trace-id: 8f3a-77c1b - timeline: submit->start(10ms)->kv-miss->kv-fetch(120ms)->execute

If you pick this up: start with rollback (low-risk) + KV sweep disable on test cluster, and ping #serving-runtime with a short status update. Attach microbench results to JIRA INF-8421.

-- maya
